rationale: origin/main advanced by two commits that touch three files this PLAN edits: #278 (fix(execute): unblock the single-pr path on macOS) rewrote plan-to-tasks.sh's associative arrays and nameref into bash 3.2-compatible tab-string helpers, replaced a GNU-only sed form in slugify, and restructured check-plan-scripts.yml so its macOS leg runs /bin/bash explicitly; #284 (ci(lifecycle)) made the whole-tree lifecycle gate actually run and cleared the orphan PRD it revealed. Neither invalidates the PLAN's foundation. Every design decision survives unchanged: the single walk, the shirabe plan outlines subcommand, the FC17 promotion, the notice/error boundary, and the binary-resolution ladder are all untouched by these commits. What changed is implementation detail inside the file Issue 4 edits, plus two consequences worth recording. First, plan-to-tasks.sh is now under a bash 3.2 compatibility contract enforced by a real cross-version CI matrix, so Issue 4's rewrite must avoid declare -A, namerefs, and GNU-only sed forms; this is an added constraint on how Issue 4 is implemented, not a change to what it must achieve, and the PLAN's Issue 4 outline is amended in place to name it. Second, two of the four tooling defects the task brief said to work around are now fixed upstream: the worktree-discipline gate's unset PLAN_SLUG (#270) is a declared template variable, and the lifecycle CI workflow (#282) runs. The PLAN's own task graph was re-extracted against the rewritten extractor after the rebase and still matches its four declared edges.
